title: Two telescope samples show no clear excess fluence similarity between consecutive groups of FRB 20220912A
abstract: We test whether consecutive detected burst groups have similar fluences in two public samples of FRB 20220912A. The test compares squared log-fluence differences with within-session shuffles. CHIME Catalog 2 gives a roughness ratio of 1.212 in 47 pairs from nine sessions, with a lower-tail shuffle probability of 0.949. Nancay gives 0.980 in 550 pairs from 27 sessions, with probability 0.334. Neither sample shows clear excess similarity. Wait cuts, close-burst grouping, time splits, and an Nancay high-signal cut retain this result. The Nancay result supports an earlier published null test. A fixed-layout simulation detects a latent correlation of 0.3 in 99.35 percent of Nancay trials but only 26.65 percent of CHIME trials. This simulation does not include missing bursts or the detection pipeline. Band-limited fluence need not trace released energy. No new source or physical signal is confirmed. The package contains original code, aggregate results, source hashes, a figure, and retrieval steps. External source rows are not bundled.

display.caption: Adjacent log-fluence roughness divided by its session-shuffle expectation. Values below one indicate similarity. Bars give nominal whole-session bootstrap intervals. The CHIME high-signal cut has no eligible session. Time removal uses an approximate residual shuffle.

citations.reason: Earlier Nancay consecutive-fluence null result. This work adds conditional session shuffles, grouping controls, and an independent CHIME sample.
